facts.text: It's on the left side, at my temple.
I've had it for a month.
I've noticed I can't see out to the sides, on the outer side of both eyes.
I've had high blood pressure for more than 20 years.
Apart from high blood pressure, I don't have any other medical problems.
I've never had an autoimmune disease.
No one in my family has had an autoimmune disease.

findings.name: serum biochemistry
findings.result: Potassium 3.2 mmol/L; other biochemical tests within normal limits.

findings.name: autoimmune antibodies
findings.result: Antinuclear antibodies negative; no antithyroid antibodies.

findings.name: serum immunoglobulins
findings.result: IgG, IgM, IgA and IgG4: negative.

findings.name: pituitary hormone evaluation
findings.result: Hypothalamic–pituitary–adrenal axis: deficient; thyroid axis: deficient; gonadal axis: deficient.

findings.name: MRI of the pituitary gland
findings.result: Symmetrical enlargement of the pituitary with suprasellar “dumbbell” extension; significant homogeneous enhancement after gadolinium; low signal in the anterior pituitary on T1 and high signal on T2; preserved bright spot in the posterior lobe; thickened, undeviated pituitary stalk; bilateral cavernous sinus encirclement of the internal carotid arteries; parasellar dural tail sign.

gold.reasoning: 1. Granulomatous hypophysitis considered because it can infiltrate the sella but excluded due to rarity and autopsy identification — “Although granulomatous hypophysitis could also present with similar sellar infiltration; however, granulomatous hypophysitis is very rare and often found by autopsy.” 2. Necrotizing hypophysitis considered but excluded by the presence of homogeneous contrast enhancement and absence of ischemic changes — “Necrotizing hypophysitis present with a lack of contrast enhancement and sudden-onset hypopituitarism… Our patient presented with marked homogeneous anterior pituitary enhancement without ischemic manifestations.” 3. Xanthomatous hypophysitis considered but excluded by the lack of cystic ring enhancement and known steroid responsiveness — “Xanthomatous hypophysitis commonly exhibits cystic enlargement and peripheral ring enhancement after contrast and is rarely known to improve in response to glucocorticoid therapies.”

f005: 'had worsened at night' read as the headache being worse at night (timing), not as a night-time change in course.
f007: 'She also noted' read as the patient noticing the field defects; no visual field examination result is given, so there is no finding.

x012.source_text: Magnetic resonance imaging of the pituitary gland demonstrated symmetrical enlargement with suprasellar “dumbbell” extension, significant homogeneous enhancement after gadolinium, low signal in the anterior pituitary on T1, high signal on T2, a preserved bright spot in the posterior lobe, thickening of an undeviated pituitary stalk, bilateral cavernous sinus encirclement of the internal carotid arteries, and a parasellar dural tail sign.

x007: The source says she was 'negative for' IgG, IgM, IgA and IgG4; immunoglobulins are measured as levels, so this probably means not elevated. Kept as written.
x009: The source gives no hormone values, only which axes were deficient.

source_issues: s002 reports bilateral temporal visual field defects, while s004 calls the neurological examination unremarkable; no formal visual field examination is reported.
s006: immunoglobulins (IgG, IgM, IgA, IgG4) are listed as 'negative', which is not a usual way to report levels.
notes: Index visit: the outpatient presentation with a 1-month intermittent left temporal headache and bitemporal field defects (s001-s004); all laboratory, endocrine and imaging results (s005-s010) are findings from the same workup.
x003: the neurological examination record has no visual-field alias, so a visual field request stays unavailable instead of returning 'unremarkable' against the patient's reported field loss.
s007 'Other biochemical and coagulation tests were within normal limits' supports both the biochemistry record (x004) and the coagulation record (x008).
